name: Margin Percentage
description: Calculate gross margin as a percentage of price.
business_contexts: a retailer pricing a product against its wholesale cost
a restaurant pricing a dish against ingredient cost
a manufacturer pricing a component against production cost
a service firm pricing an engagement against delivery cost
an e-commerce brand pricing an item against landed cost
question_patterns: Given the price and cost below, what is the gross margin percentage?
Calculate margin as a percentage of price from the figures given.
What percentage of price is margin, given the price and cost shown?
Calculate the gross margin rate from the price and cost given.
What gross margin percentage results from the price and cost below?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate margin percentage = (price − cost) / price × 100
key_insight: Margin percentage is always taken as a share of price, not of cost — mixing the two up is the single most common margin-math error.
common_mistakes: Dividing by cost instead of price
Reporting the dollar margin as if it were the percentage
framework_soundbite: Margin is the gap over price — cost is what you subtract, price is what you divide by.
